Results.Name: Bundled Python reads both supported layouts with exact original-byte provenance
Binary PDF transport is unchanged when the host console input encoding has a UTF-8 BOM
Python and the standard reader agree on profiles, dates, pages and verified fingerprints
Both actual readers preserve printed water/noise measurements and their explicit limits
Page, character and byte bounds remain explicit with the Python reader
Image-only and encrypted inputs remain separate from successful text extraction
An altered archived PDF is rejected before either reader can acquire new provenance
A damaged standard-reader component is rejected and automatic mode falls back to verified Python reading
An invalid Python dependency is rejected explicitly while automatic standard reading remains usable
A missing Python runtime allows automatic standard reading and a clear explicit-reader error
Cancelled reads expose no text or successful provenance and do not create analysis evidence
Current caches are reused across fresh modules and older evidence upgrades only on a selected read
Cancelling after Python starts terminates its real child process and preserves all cached evidence
The complete production archive-to-Python reader runs under an actual non-administrator token

Scope: Actual production PDF reader against generated text, image-only and encrypted PDFs. Both engines retain indexed-byte provenance; limits, changed bytes, dependency integrity, fallback and cache preservation are explicit. No hospital network, real PDF or work-computer policy is exercised by this public suite.
